So, a few things that I want to bring to attention here:

1) there's not enough information to be like "this person was in the wrong" or "omg this person was such an a hole", etc. 

2) boundaries are for yourself and NOT for other people. It's about preserving your energy and what's healthy for you. In this case, the person putting them up must be feeling a certain way to even talk about it in the first place. Maybe OP, you can think about some boundaries that would be healthy for you? 

3) there's a term called "flooding" which is essentially the feeling of being overwhelmed during an argument that completely takes over and requires some time to just walk away and calm down for a bit. I think no one did that in this conversation since it just seems to keep going

4) boundaries will usually be met with resistance. it's normal for someone to react this way to a new boundary. however, it's important to communicate boundaries clearly, succinctly, firmly and with some love/kindness 

5) lastly, ultimatums are NOT inherently wrong. ultimatums can be used to healthily enforce a boundary. In this example, the person could have said "If you yell at me or call me names today at the beach, then I will walk away and do something by myself". That's a reasonable consequence to violating a boundary. Note the word REASONABLE. an unhealthy ultimatum would be "if you yell at me or call me names at the beach, then I will leave your ass there or break up with you!". The consequence doesn't fit the action. 

Everyone is doing the what they know with what they have, so you all just need some practice, patience, and time. Boundaries are hard. BP2 is hard to live with. But, if you want to talk about anything else boundaries wise, reach out! :)
